translations.literal: The dragon ascended the northern capital, and righteous wind covered the nine domains;
translations.idiomatic: The dragon rose at the northern capital, and righteous wind spread over the nine regions;

sentences.zh: 鳳翔天域，則威聲格於八表。

translations.literal: the phoenix soared in the celestial realm, and awesome renown reached the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: the phoenix soared through the celestial realm, and commanding fame reached the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 屬奸雄鼎峙之秋，群凶嶽立之際，昧旦臨朝，日旰忘膳，運籌命將，舉無遺策。

translations.literal: It fell in the season when treacherous heroes stood like tripods and wicked chiefs rose like peaks; he attended court before dawn and forgot his meal at sunset, laid plans and appointed generals, and in every move no stratagem was left aside.
translations.idiomatic: It was the season when traitor-heroes stood like tripods and wicked chiefs towered like peaks. He held court before dawn and at sunset still forgot his meal; he plotted and appointed commanders, and in every move left no stratagem unused.

sentences.zh: 親禦六戎，則有征無戰。

translations.literal: When he personally took the six armies in hand, there was campaign but no battle.
translations.idiomatic: When he himself took the six hosts in hand, there was expedition but no fighting.

sentences.zh: 故偽秦以三世之資，喪魂于關、隴；

translations.literal: Therefore the false Qin, with three generations' resources, lost its soul at Guan and Long;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the false Qin, with the wealth of three generations, lost heart at Guan and Long;

sentences.zh: 河源望旗而委質，北虜欽風而納款。

translations.literal: the He source saw the banners and submitted; the northern barbarians revered the wind and tendered allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: the He source beheld his banners and surrendered allegiance; the northern tribes, awed by his wind, came in with tribute.

sentences.zh: 德音著於柔服，威刑彰於伐叛，文教與武功並宣，俎豆與干戈俱運。

translations.literal: Virtuous sound was manifest in gentle submission; stern punishment was displayed in punishing rebellion; civil teaching and martial achievement were proclaimed together, ritual vessels and weapons moved as one.
translations.idiomatic: His virtuous renown showed in those who yielded peacefully; his stern law showed in those he punished for rebellion. Civil teaching and martial achievement were spread together; ritual and arms advanced as one.

sentences.zh: 五稔之間，道風弘著，暨乎七載而王猷允洽。

translations.literal: Within five harvests the Way's wind was broadly displayed; by the seventh year the royal plan was fully harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Within five harvests the Way's influence stood forth in splendor; by the seventh year the royal design was wholly brought to accord.

sentences.zh: 乃遠惟周文，啟經始之基；

translations.literal: Then looking far to King Wen of Zhou, he opened the foundation of beginning;
translations.idiomatic: He looked far back to King Wen of Zhou, who laid the foundation of beginning;

sentences.zh: 近詳山川，究形勝之地，遂營起都城，開建京邑。

translations.literal: examining near the mountains and rivers, he investigated terrain of strategic advantage, and thereupon raised a capital city and opened an imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: and near at hand studied mountains and rivers, tracing ground of strategic mastery—then raised a capital and opened an imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 背名山而面洪流，左河津而右重塞。

translations.literal: Backed by famous mountains and facing a mighty flood, with the river ford on the left and heavy passes on the right.
translations.idiomatic: It backed on famous mountains and faced a mighty river, with the ford on the left and layered passes on the right.

sentences.zh: 高隅隱日，崇墉際雲，石郭天池，周綿千里。

translations.literal: High corners hid the sun; lofty walls met the clouds; stone outer works and a moat like heaven's pool encircled a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: High battlements hid the sun; towering ramparts touched the clouds; stone walls and a heaven-like moat ran a thousand li round.

sentences.zh: 其為獨守之形，險絕之狀，固以遠邁於咸陽，超美于周洛，若乃廣五郊之義，尊七廟之制，崇左社之規，建右稷之禮，禦太一以繕明堂，模帝坐而營路寢，閶闔披霄而山亭，象魏排虛而岳峙，華林靈沼，崇台秘室，通房連閣，馳道苑園，可以陰映萬邦，光覆四海，莫不鬱然並建，森然畢備，若紫微之帶皇穹，閬風之跨后土。

translations.literal: In its form of solitary defense and its aspect of extreme peril, it far surpassed Xianyang and excelled Zhou and Luo. Moreover he extended the rites of the five suburbs, honored the system of seven temples, exalted the rule of the left altar of soil, established the rite of the right grain god, addressed Taiyi in repairing the Bright Hall, modeled the Emperor's Seat in building the Road Chamber; Chongmen opened the sky like mountain pavilions, the Image Towers stood void like peaks; Flowery Forest and Spirit Pool, lofty terraces and secret chambers, connecting rooms and linked pavilions, racing ways and park gardens—all could cast shadow over ten thousand states and spread light over the four seas; none were not richly raised together, densely completed, like the Purple Enclosure girdling the imperial vault or Langfeng spanning the rear earth.
translations.idiomatic: In form a fortress that none could share, in aspect peril pushed to the utmost, it far outran Xianyang and outshone Zhou and Luo. He widened the rites of the five suburbs, honored the seven-temple system, exalted the left altar of soil, established the right grain altar, addressed Taiyi in repairing the Bright Hall, and modeled the Emperor's Seat in building the Road Chamber. Chongmen gates pierced the sky like mountain pavilions; the Image Towers rose void as peaks. Flowery Forest and Spirit Pool, lofty terraces and hidden chambers, linked chambers and continuous galleries, racing tracks and royal parks—all could cast shadow over ten thousand states and spread radiance across the four seas. Nothing was left unbuilt in splendor, nothing unfinished in density—like the Purple Enclosure girdling the vault of heaven, like Langfeng spanning the earth below.

sentences.zh: 然宰司鼎臣，群黎士庶，僉以為重威之式，有闕前王。

translations.literal: Yet chief ministers and the mass of officials and commoners all said that in the model of august majesty something was lacking compared with former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet chief ministers, officials, and commoners alike held that in the pattern of august majesty something still fell short of former kings.

sentences.zh: 於是延王爾之奇工，命班輸之妙匠，搜文梓于鄧林，采繡石于恆嶽，九域貢以金銀，八方獻其瑰寶，親運神奇，參制規矩，營離宮於露寢之南，起別殿于永安之北。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned the marvelous craftsmen of Wang Er, commanded the subtle artisans of Ban Shu, sought patterned catalpa in Deng Forest and gathered brocade stone on Mount Heng; the nine domains presented gold and silver, the eight directions offered their rare treasures; he personally wielded wonder and joined in setting compass and square, built a detached palace south of the Dew Chamber and raised a separate hall north of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the wondrous craftsmen of Wang Er and commanded the subtle artisans of Ban Shu; he sought patterned catalpa in Deng Forest and gathered brocade stone from Mount Heng. The nine domains sent gold and silver; the eight directions offered rare treasures. He himself directed wonder and shared in setting compass and square, built a detached palace south of the Dew Chamber, and raised a separate hall north of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 高構千尋，崇基萬仞。

translations.literal: The upper structure reached a thousand ren; the foundation rose ten thousand ren.
translations.idiomatic: Its upper works climbed a thousand ren; its foundation rose ten thousand ren.

sentences.zh: 玄棟鏤榥，若騰虹之揚眉；

translations.literal: Dark beams and carved brackets were like a soaring rainbow lifting its brow;
translations.idiomatic: Dark beams and carved brackets arched like a rainbow rearing its brow;

sentences.zh: 飛簷舒咢，似翔鵬之矯翼。

translations.literal: flying eaves spread their beaks like a soaring peng bending its wings.
translations.idiomatic: flying eaves spread their beaks like a soaring peng folding its wings.

sentences.zh: 二序啟矣，而五時之坐開；

translations.literal: The two wings opened, and seats for the five seasons were laid out;
translations.idiomatic: The two wings opened, and seats for the five seasons were set out;

sentences.zh: 四隅陳設，而一禦之位建。

translations.literal: the four corners were arrayed, and the single imperial seat was established.
translations.idiomatic: the four corners were furnished, and the one imperial seat was raised.

sentences.zh: 溫宮膠葛，涼殿崢嶸，絡以隋珠，綷以金鏡，雖曦望互升於表，而中無晝夜之殊；

translations.literal: Warm palaces intertwined, cool halls stood rugged; strung with Sui pearls and woven with gold mirrors—though dawn and dusk alternated above, within there was no difference of day and night;
translations.idiomatic: Warm palaces wound into one another; cool halls rose rugged. Strung with Sui pearls, woven with gold mirrors—though dawn and dusk took turns outside, within there was neither day nor night;

sentences.zh: 陰陽迭更於外，而內無寒暑之別。

translations.literal: yin and yang alternated without, yet within there was no distinction of cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: yin and yang shifted without, yet within there was no difference of cold and heat.

sentences.zh: 故善目者不能為其名，博辯者不能究其稱，斯蓋神明之所規模，非人工之所經制。

translations.literal: Therefore keen eyes could not name it, and eloquent debaters could not exhaust its designations—this was surely a pattern laid by the spirits, not a structure that human hands could compass.
translations.idiomatic: Keen eyes could not name it; eloquent tongues could not exhaust its titles. Surely this was a design laid by the spirits—not a thing human hands could compass.

sentences.zh: 若乃尋名以求類，蹤狀以效真，據質以究名，形疑妙出，雖如來、須彌之寶塔，帝釋、忉利之神宮，尚未足以喻其麗，方其飾矣。

translations.literal: If one sought its kind by tracing names, matched form by following traces, investigated names by substance, and form seemed to issue from wonder—even the treasure pagodas of the Tathagata and Mount Sumeru, the spirit palaces of Shakra and Trayastrimsha, would not suffice to image its beauty when it was adorned.
translations.idiomatic: Seek its kind by name, match form to trace, weigh substance against title, and the shape seems born of wonder itself—even the treasure towers of the Tathagata on Mount Sumeru, the spirit palaces of Shakra in Trayastrimsha, could not suffice to picture its splendor once adorned.

sentences.zh: 昔周宣考室而詠于詩人，閟宮有侐而頌聲是作。

translations.literal: Of old King Xuan of Zhou examined his chamber and the poets sang; the solemn palace stood vast and the hymn was made.
translations.idiomatic: Of old King Xuan of Zhou examined his chamber and the poets sang of it; when the solemn palace stood vast, a hymn was raised.

sentences.zh: 況乃太微肇制，清都啟建，軌一文昌，舊章唯始，咸秩百神，賓享萬國，群生開其耳目，天下詠其來蘇，亦何得不播之管弦，刊之金石哉！

translations.literal: How much more when the Supreme Palace first established its system and the Clear Capital opened its founding—one track with the Palace of Literature, old statutes only now begun, all ranks of spirits ordered, ten thousand states received as guests, all living things opened their eyes and ears, and the realm sang of returning life—how could this not be spread on pipes and strings and carved in metal and stone!
translations.idiomatic: How much more now, when the Supreme Palace first framed its rule and the Clear Capital opened its founding—one track with the Palace of Literature, ancient statutes begun anew, the hundred spirits ordered in rank, ten thousand states feasted as guests, all creatures opening eyes and ears, the realm singing of restored life—how could it not be carried on pipes and strings, cut into bronze and stone!

sentences.zh: 乃樹銘都邑，敷贊碩美，俾皇風振于來葉，聖庸垂乎不朽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set up an inscription in the capital and spread praise of great beauty, so that imperial wind would stir in coming generations and sage merit hang immortal.
translations.idiomatic: He set up an inscription in the capital and spread praise of its greatness, that imperial wind might stir in ages to come and sage achievement hang immortal.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: The text says:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: 於赫靈祚，配乾比靈斯。

translations.literal: Splendid is the imperial fortune, matching Qian and rivaling the numinous—thus!
translations.idiomatic: Splendid the imperial fortune, paired with Heaven, equal to the numinous—

sentences.zh: 巍巍大禹，堂堂聖功。

translations.literal: Vast, vast is Great Yu; grand, grand his sage achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Vast, vast Great Yu; grand, grand his sage works.

sentences.zh: 仁被蒼生，德格玄穹。

translations.literal: Benevolence covered the black-haired people; virtue reached the dark vault.
translations.idiomatic: His benevolence covered the living; his virtue reached the dark heavens.

sentences.zh: 帝錫玄珪，揖讓受終。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed the dark scepter; by yielding he received the end.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted the dark scepter; by yielding he received the mandate.

sentences.zh: 哲王繼軌，光闡徽風。

translations.literal: Sage kings followed in one track; they brightly spread the fine wind.
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings followed in one track; they spread the fine wind in splendor.

sentences.zh: 道無常夷，數或不競。

translations.literal: The Way is not always level; the count sometimes does not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The Way is not always smooth; fate sometimes fails to favor.

sentences.zh: 金精南邁，天輝北映。

translations.literal: Metal essence moved south; celestial glory shone north.
translations.idiomatic: Metal's essence moved south; heaven's glory mirrored north.

sentences.zh: 靈祉逾昌，世葉彌盛。

translations.literal: Numinous blessing grew ever fuller; the generations' branches flourished more.
translations.idiomatic: Numinous blessing grew ever greater; the branches of the line flourished more.

sentences.zh: 惟祖惟父，克廣休命。

translations.literal: Our forefathers and fathers broadened the great mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Forefathers and fathers broadened the great mandate.

sentences.zh: 如彼日月，連光接鏡。

translations.literal: Like sun and moon, their light joined and their mirrors met.
translations.idiomatic: Like sun and moon, their light joined, their mirrors met.

sentences.zh: 玄符瑞德，乾運有歸。

translations.literal: The dark talisman and auspicious virtue—Heaven's motion had its return.
translations.idiomatic: Dark omen and auspicious virtue—Heaven's turning had its return.

sentences.zh: 誕鐘我後，應圖龍飛。

translations.literal: It bore and rang out our lord; he answered the chart and the dragon flew.
translations.idiomatic: It bore and rang for our lord; he answered the chart and the dragon rose.

sentences.zh: 落落神武，恢恢聖姿。

translations.literal: Clear, clear his divine martial bearing; vast, vast his sage presence.
translations.idiomatic: Clear, clear his divine martial air; vast, vast his sage bearing.

sentences.zh: 名教內敷，群妖外夷。

translations.literal: Within, the name-teachings spread; without, the many demons were leveled.
translations.idiomatic: Within, the teachings of names spread; without, the demon hordes were leveled.

sentences.zh: 化光四表，威截九圍。

translations.literal: His transforming light reached the four quarters; his awesomeness cut the nine domains.
translations.idiomatic: Transforming light reached the four quarters; awesomeness cut the nine domains.

sentences.zh: 封畿之制，王者常經。

translations.literal: The system of the royal domain is the constant canon of kings.
translations.idiomatic: The royal domain's design is the constant law of kings.

sentences.zh: 乃延輸、爾，肇建帝京。

translations.literal: Then he summoned Shu and Er and first built the imperial capital.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Shu and Er and first raised the imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 土苞上壤，地跨勝形。

translations.literal: Its soil embraced the upper soil; its ground crossed winning terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Its soil embraced the upper realm; its ground spanned winning ground.

sentences.zh: 庶人子來，不日而成。

translations.literal: The common people came like sons; in no many days it was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Common folk came like sons; in no many days it stood complete.

sentences.zh: 崇台霄峙，秀闕雲亭。

translations.literal: Lofty terraces stood in the clouds; elegant gates rose cloud-high.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty terraces stood in the clouds; elegant gates towered cloud-high.

sentences.zh: 千榭連隅，萬閣接屏。

translations.literal: A thousand pavilions linked corner to corner; ten thousand towers joined screen to screen.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand pavilions linked corner to corner; ten thousand towers joined screen to screen.

sentences.zh: 晃若晨曦，昭若列星。

translations.literal: Bright as morning light; clear as ranks of stars.
translations.idiomatic: Bright as morning light; clear as ordered stars.

sentences.zh: 離宮既作，別宇雲施。

translations.literal: The detached palace was made; separate halls spread like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The detached palace was built; separate halls spread like clouds.

sentences.zh: 爰構崇明，仰准乾儀。

translations.literal: Then he built Chongming, looking up to the pattern of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He built Chongming, looking up to the pattern of Qian.

sentences.zh: 懸薨風閱，飛軒雲垂。

translations.literal: Suspended beams and wind-pavilions; flying galleries hung like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Suspended beams and wind-pavilions; flying galleries hung cloud-low.

sentences.zh: 溫室嵯峨，層城參差。

translations.literal: Warm chambers stood rugged; layered walls rose uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Warm chambers towered rugged; layered walls rose in tiers.

sentences.zh: 楹雕虯獸，節鏤龍螭。

translations.literal: Columns carved with horned beasts; nodes chased with dragon wyrms.
translations.idiomatic: Columns carved with horned beasts; nodes chased with dragon wyrms.

sentences.zh: 瑩以寶璞，飾以珍奇。

translations.literal: Polished with precious jade; adorned with rare wonders.
translations.idiomatic: Polished with precious jade; adorned with rare wonders.

sentences.zh: 稱因褒著，名由實揚。

translations.literal: The name follows praise made manifest; the name rises from substance displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Its title follows praise made manifest; its name rises from substance shown.

sentences.zh: 偉哉皇室，盛矣厥章！

translations.literal: Great is the imperial house; splendid its emblem!
translations.idiomatic: Great the imperial house; splendid its emblem!

sentences.zh: 義高靈台，美隆未央。

translations.literal: Its righteousness towers above the Spirit Terrace; its beauty surpasses Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Its righteousness towers above the Spirit Terrace; its beauty outdoes Weiyang.

sentences.zh: 邁軌三五，貽則霸王。

translations.literal: It passes the tracks of the Three and Five; it bequeaths models to hegemons and kings.
translations.idiomatic: It passes the measure of the Three and Five; it bequeaths models to hegemons and kings.

sentences.zh: 永世垂節，億載彌光。

translations.literal: For eternal ages its standards hang; for a hundred million years its light spreads.
translations.idiomatic: For eternal ages its standards hang; for a hundred million years its light spreads.

sentences.zh: 其秘書監胡義周之辭也。

translations.literal: These were the words of Secretariat Director Hu Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: This was the text composed by Hu Yizhou, Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 名其南門曰朝宋門，東門曰招魏門，西門曰服涼門，北門曰平朔門。

translations.literal: He named the southern gate Chaosong Gate, the eastern gate Zhaowei Gate, the western gate Fuliang Gate, and the northern gate Pingshuo Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He named the southern gate Chaosong, the eastern Zhaowei, the western Fuliang, and the northern Pingshuo.

sentences.zh: 追尊其高祖訓兒曰元皇帝，曾祖武曰景皇帝，祖豹子曰宣皇帝，父衛辰曰桓皇帝，廟號太祖，母苻氏曰桓文皇后。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his great-grandfather Xun'er as Emperor Yuan, his grandfather Wu as Emperor Jing, his grandfather Baozi as Emperor Xuan, and his father Weichen as Emperor Huan; the temple name was Taizu, and his mother, Lady Fu, was Empress Huanwen.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his great-grandfather Xun'er as Emperor Yuan, his grandfather Wu as Emperor Jing, his grandfather Baozi as Emperor Xuan, and his father Weichen as Emperor Huan, with temple name Taizu; his mother, the Fu clan, was Empress Huanwen.

sentences.zh: 勃勃性凶暴好殺，無順守之規。

translations.literal: Bobo by nature was fierce, cruel, and fond of killing; he had no rule of compliant preservation.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Bobo was savage, cruel, and murderous; he observed no law of gentle rule.

sentences.zh: 常居城上，置弓劍於側，有所嫌忿，便手自殺之，群臣忤視者毀其目，笑者決其脣，諫者謂之誹謗，先截其舌而後斬之。

translations.literal: He constantly stayed atop the wall, with bow and sword at his side; when he bore resentment he would personally kill the man. Officials who met his gaze with defiance had their eyes destroyed; those who laughed had their lips cut; remonstrators he called slanderers—first he cut out the tongue, then beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly kept to the ramparts, bow and sword at his side. When angered, he killed with his own hand. Ministers who met his eye with defiance had their eyes put out; those who laughed had their lips slit; remonstrators he called slanderers—he cut out the tongue first, then beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 夷夏囂然，人無生賴。

translations.literal: Barbarian and Chinese alike were in uproar; men had no means to live.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian and Chinese alike were in uproar; no one could count on life.

sentences.zh: 在位十三年而宋受禪，以宋元嘉二年死。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of his reign the Song received the mandate; he died in the second year of Yuanjia of the Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of his reign the Song received the mandate; he died in Song Yuanjia year two.

sentences.zh: 子昌嗣偽位，尋為魏所擒。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded to the false throne and was soon captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded to the false throne and was soon taken by Wei.

sentences.zh: 弟定僭號於平涼，遂為魏所滅。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ding usurped the title at Pingliang and was thereupon destroyed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ding seized the title at Pingliang and was in turn destroyed by Wei.

sentences.zh: 自勃勃至定，凡二十有六載而亡。

translations.literal: From Bobo to Ding, altogether twenty-six years and they perished.
translations.idiomatic: From Bobo to Ding, twenty-six years in all—and the house was gone.

sentences.zh: 【評贊】

translations.literal: [Appraisal]
translations.idiomatic: [Appraisal]

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：赫連勃勃犬熏醜種類，入居邊宇，屬中壤分崩，緣間肆慝，控弦鳴鏑，據有朔方。

translations.literal: The historian says: Helian Bobo was of the dog-stench, ugly breed; he entered and dwelt in the border lands. When the central realm split apart, he seized the interval and unleashed wickedness; controlling bowstrings and sounding arrows, he held the northern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Helian Bobo was of that dog-stench, ugly stock. He entered the borderlands; when the central realm split apart, he seized the breach and unleashed wickedness. With bow at the ready and whistling arrows, he held the northern wilds.

sentences.zh: 遂乃法玄象以開宮，擬神京而建社，竊先王之徽號，備中國之禮容，驅駕英賢，窺窬天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the dark signs to open his palace, modeled the divine capital to establish his altar, stole the august titles of former kings, and equipped himself with the ritual and bearing of China; driving heroes and worthies, he peered and coveted the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He took the dark signs to open his palace, modeled the divine capital to raise his altar, stole the august titles of former kings, and arrayed himself in the ritual and bearing of China—driving heroes and worthies while peering and coveting the realm.

sentences.zh: 然其器識高爽，風骨魁奇，姚興睹之而醉心，宋祖聞之而動色。

translations.literal: Yet his capacity and insight were lofty and clear, his wind and bone outstanding and strange; Yao Xing saw him and was intoxicated in heart, and Emperor Wu of Song heard of him and was moved in countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his capacity and insight were lofty and keen, his bearing outstanding and strange. Yao Xing saw him and lost his heart to him; Emperor Wu of Song heard of him and changed color.

sentences.zh: 豈陰山之韞異氣，不然何以致斯乎！

translations.literal: Could it be that the Yin Mountains hoard a strange breath—if not, how else could he have reached this?
translations.idiomatic: Did the Yin Mountains hoard some strange breath—if not, how else could he have come to this?

sentences.zh: 雖雄略過人，而凶殘未革，飾非距諫，酷害朝臣，部內囂然，忠良捲舌。

translations.literal: Though his heroic strategy surpassed others, his fierce cruelty was not reformed; he whitewashed faults and rejected remonstrance, cruelly harmed court ministers, and within his domains there was uproar—loyal and good men curled their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Though his heroic strategy surpassed others, his savagery was never reformed. He masked faults and rejected counsel, cruelly harmed court ministers, and within his domains there was uproar—loyal men bit their tongues.

sentences.zh: 滅亡之禍，宜在厥身，猶及其嗣，非不幸也。

translations.literal: The calamity of extinction should have fallen on his person; that it reached even his heirs was not misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The calamity of extinction ought to have fallen on him alone; that it reached even his heirs was no accident.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：淳維遠裔，名王之餘。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Chunwei's distant descendant, remnant of the royal name-clan.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Chunwei's distant descendant, remnant of a royal line.

sentences.zh: 嘯群龍漠，乘釁侵漁。

translations.literal: He howled with the dragon herds of the desert and seized the chance to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: He howled with the dragon herds of the desert and seized the chance to raid and harry.

sentences.zh: 爰創宮宇，易彼氈廬。

translations.literal: Then he created palaces and halls and changed those felt tents.
translations.idiomatic: Then he raised palaces and halls and changed those felt tents for stone.

sentences.zh: 雖弄神器，猶曰凶渠。

translations.literal: Although he wielded the regalia of empire, he was still called a vicious chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though he wielded the regalia of empire, he was still reckoned a murderous brigand-chieftain.
